title: Binary Search
statement:
Find a value in a **sorted** array of integers and return its index.

## Your function

```
int binary_search(const int *values, int count, int target);
```

Return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present. `values` is
sorted in ascending order.

## Watch out

- Halve the search range each step. A linear scan passes these tests
  but misses the point of the exercise.
- `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` avoids the overflow that `(lo + hi) / 2` can hit
  on large arrays.
- Getting the loop condition wrong here usually means an infinite loop
  rather than a wrong answer, so the tests have a time limit.
- `count` may be `0`, in which case `values` may be `NULL`.

tests.name: last element
tests.description: A common off-by-one: `high` must start at count-1 and the loop must still run when low == high.

tests.name: empty array
tests.description: Must return -1 without reading through a NULL pointer.
